title: New bounds for double covers of the discrete box {0,1,2}^d
summary: A proper sub-box of $A=\{0,1,2\}^d$ is a product $S_1\times\dots\times S_d$ with each $\varnothing\neq S_i\subsetneq\{0,1,2\}$. A double cover is a finite multiset of proper sub-boxes covering every point of $A$ exactly twice; write $f(d)$ for the minimum size of a double cover. Leader, Milicevic and Tan asked whether $f(d)\ge 2^d$ for all $d$ (Question 4.1 of the PatternBoost paper of Charton-Ellenberg-Wagner-Williamson), analogous to the Alon-Bohman-Holzman-Kleitman partition bound $2^d$. No better than the trivial volume bound was previously known, for any $d\ge 2$. We prove the first…
